title: Teaching with ChatGPT as a Linguistically Responsive Tool for Multilingual Learners
extended_summary:
This study examines how teachers of K–12 multilingual learners in U.S. public schools are using ChatGPT and related AI tools to support language and literacy instruction. The paper is motivated by concerns about how generative AI is actually implemented in real classrooms, especially for multilingual learners whose linguistic resources are often marginalized by monolingual school norms. Using a translanguaging lens, the study asks how teachers use ChatGPT in instructional practice and whether those uses support linguistically responsive pedagogy.

The study draws on classroom observations and post-observation interviews with in-service teachers enrolled in a professional development course on culturally and linguistically responsive pedagogy. Across two cohorts over two academic years, the researcher observed 42 teachers in DC public and charter schools; instances of ChatGPT use were identified in 8 observations. The observed teachers worked across elementary and secondary levels and across content areas including general education, ESL, dual-language bilingual education, Spanish immersion, science, math, and English language arts.

Findings show that teachers mainly used ChatGPT to facilitate communication and differentiate content, such as translating text, generating bilingual explanations, transcribing oral language, simplifying or re-leveling texts, and creating exemplar disciplinary writing models. In a smaller number of secondary classrooms, teachers also scaffolded students’ own prompting of ChatGPT and experimented with Dall-E for multimodal literacy activities. The paper concludes that ChatGPT can support translanguaging affordances, production, and some co-labor, but that assessment and reflection were notably absent. It also emphasizes the need for explicit teacher mediation, critical AI literacy, and safeguards against bias, overreliance, and inappropriate or inaccurate outputs.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI system that generates and transforms text and other outputs from prompts; here used for translation, text simplification/differentiation, transcription, prompt scaffolding, and image generation via DALL·E integration.
identified_tools.use_case: Observed in K–12 multilingual learner classrooms and teacher interviews as a teacher-facing tool to translate texts and vocabulary, transcribe and translate student speech, create differentiated and leveled texts, generate exemplar disciplinary texts, scaffold student prompting for writing support, and support a multimodal literacy activity using image generation.

findings.finding_summary: Across 42 observed K–12 teachers, ChatGPT was used in 8 observations to support language and literacy instruction for multilingual learners. Reported classroom uses included translation, transcription, text differentiation, prompt scaffolding, and a multimodal image-generation activity; the paper reports no experimental effect sizes or test-score outcomes.
findings.measure: Classroom-observed instructional uses of ChatGPT in literacy/language teaching
findings.sample_size: n=42 observed teachers; 8 observations with ChatGPT use

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative classroom-observation study with post-observation interviews, not an experimental or quasi-experimental impact study. It provides implementation evidence, but no causal evidence or quantified learning effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially meaningful instructional uses of ChatGPT for multilingual literacy support, but it reports no effect sizes or student outcome data. Impact is therefore promising but unquantified.
